brief: A seven-cell honeycomb standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet.

requirements.evidence: Seven full bases at level 0: centre piece:0,0,0;full ringed by piece:-1,0,0, piece:-1,1,0, piece:0,-1,0, piece:0,1,0, piece:1,-1,0, piece:1,0,0 — one connected honeycomb group per check_build.

Four stud-variant spikes with facing down at level 0 junctions (e.g. spike:0#-1,0|0,-1|0,0, spike:0#0,-1|0,0|1,-1, spike:0#-1,1|0,0|0,1, spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0), spread around the cluster as feet — exceeds the minimum of three.
requirements.requirement: Standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet

finish.summary: Built a seven-cell honeycomb (one centre full base ringed by six) standing on four downward-facing stud spikes at the interior junctions, capped all open faces and bolted the joints. check_build passes with meshClash clear and a single connected group.

lines.label: M6 brass heat-set insert, 7.6 mm (initeq M6-1.0 Short)
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Building your seven-cell honeycomb on stud-spike feet — first checking what's on the bench and where the bases and spikes fit.

result.note: A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

events.text: One cell is already down; I'll place the six around it to complete the seven-cell honeycomb.
